Mom and dad hugged them and told them not to worry. They said the moon was not split. It was just a trick of the light. They said it was called a lunar eclipse. They said it was when the earth came between the sun and the moon. They said it would not last long.

Lila and Tom felt better. They went back outside with mom and dad. They watched the moon change color. It became red, then orange, then yellow, then green. It was like a rainbow. Lila and Tom liked the green moon. They thought it was pretty. They said it was their favorite color.

They stayed outside until the moon was round again. They said good night to the moon and the stars. They went to bed and dreamed of green moons. They were happy.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Sam and Jackie. They often went out to play together. One day they decided to go rafting in the river. Sam had a regular old raft, but Jackie had a very special raft that changed colour every few minutes.

Sam was amazed. "How does it do that?" he wondered.

"It has something special inside," Jackie explained. "It keeps changing so the raft can't stay the same. It must change and move forward."

Sam thought about this. "Maybe I can change too," he said.

Jackie smiled. "Yes, we can all keep changing to go forward in life!"

The two of them continued to float down the river while Sam thought about what Jackie had said. He realised that, although it was nice to stay the same, sometimes we have to change so that we can keep moving forward. 

The moral of the story is that it's important to be open to change, so that we can keep moving towards our goals. Even if it's hard or challenging, change can help us to grow and become better!

Lila nodded. She learned a lesson that day. She decided to question everything from then on. She and Sam hopped away from the carrot and the hunter. They found some berries and nuts to eat instead. They were happy and safe.

Paul smiled at the coins, but before he knew it, the door opened. His mom was standing there. She saw the coins scattered on the floor and said, "Paul, you shouldn't take something that doesn't belong to you."
